shots.name: Student crossing out B.Com
shots.visual: Student holds a paper list, strikes a line through 'B.Com' with a pen.

storySpine.startingBelief: B.Com is purely for accounting and excludes management.
storySpine.studentSituation: The student is researching degree options and has crossed B.Com off their shortlist.
storySpine.observation: They find 'Business Organization & Management' listed in the Sem I syllabus of both Joy University B.Com Accounting & Finance (p.5) and BBA Entrepreneurship Management (p.9) for 2025-26 cohorts.
storySpine.focus: The assumption that degree titles act as rigid barriers to course content.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: If the same course title appears in both, the title alone cannot define the exclusion of management topics.
storySpine.changedAction: They restore B.Com to their provisional list for further verification.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: They move the B.Com application link from 'rejected' to 'pending review' while marking 'depth/assessment' as unknown criteria.
storySpine.channelExperience: A clear visual comparison of two PDF pages that challenges a binary classification, encouraging the viewer to look for actual module lists rather than relying on degree titles.

selected.title: Title vs. Syllabus Check
selected.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles dictate the presence of specific subjects without checking actual module lists.
selected.hlni: Business Organization & Management is listed in Semester I of the published JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management documents whose covers say students admitted from 2025–26 onwards.
selected.viewerChange: From excluding degrees based on titles to investigating actual course module lists.
selected.support: Official JOY University PDF, B.Com Accounting & Finance p.5 and BBA Entrepreneurship Management p.9; covers identify the 2025–26-onwards cohort.
methodSteps: Identify the specific programme and document cohort.
Show the inspected course-title row in each source.
Use this bounded overlap to investigate the full course, rather than assume degree titles partition subjects.
selected.interpretationRule: The supplied rows establish this shared title in these two documents only; they do not establish identical teaching, depth, assessment or availability.
selected.visibleProof: Two real cited rows correct a title-based assumption while retaining programme/version scope.
selected.payoff: A more accurate, evidence-backed list of potential academic paths.
selected.limitations: No universal overlap, identical content, exclusivity, current-admissions or career inference. BBA later sections are inconsistent; use only the inspected row.
